# BroCODE

> BroCODE is an AI-assisted coding workspace for editable source, reviewable changes and local projects (V3). AI proposals are reviewable diffs; local edits are preserved; local checkpoints allow restoring earlier versions; files export as ZIP or JSON (exports omit conversation and snapshot history); the mobile static preview is script-disabled HTML inspection; source is sent for AI help only with explicit consent. The Android release is in preparation; pricing has not been announced.

Last updated: 2026-11-02

## Guides

- [Getting started](https://codingagent.in/guides/getting-started/): Start with BroCODE: choose a first project, understand the workspace of real files, checkpoints and reviewable AI diffs, and build a repeatable idea-to-source workflow.
  - [First AI coding project ideas that you can actually finish](https://codingagent.in/guides/getting-started/first-ai-coding-project-ideas/): Beginner-friendly AI coding project ideas — portfolio, landing page, creative experiment — chosen so you can finish, preview and export them.
  - [Understanding the BroCODE workspace: files, AI help and checkpoints](https://codingagent.in/guides/getting-started/understanding-the-workspace/): How the BroCODE workspace fits together: real source files, AI proposals as reviewable diffs, local checkpoints and ZIP/JSON exports.
  - [A repeatable idea-to-source workflow for AI-assisted coding](https://codingagent.in/guides/getting-started/idea-to-source-workflow/): A six-step, repeatable idea-to-source loop for AI-assisted coding: describe, propose, review, apply, checkpoint, export.
  - [What BroCODE V3 does and does not do: setting expectations](https://codingagent.in/guides/getting-started/setting-expectations-v3/): Clear expectations for BroCODE V3: what is supported (files, diffs, checkpoints, exports, consent) and current limits (static preview, Android release in preparation).
- [Prompting for code](https://codingagent.in/guides/prompting-for-code/): How to prompt an AI for code: name the files, state constraints, add acceptance criteria and keep each request small enough to review as a diff.
  - [Acceptance criteria for AI coding prompts](https://codingagent.in/guides/prompting-for-code/acceptance-criteria-for-ai-prompts/): How to write acceptance criteria for AI coding prompts, with templates for layout, content, accessibility and scope checks you can verify in a diff.
  - [Scoping AI code changes to specific files](https://codingagent.in/guides/prompting-for-code/scoping-ai-code-changes-to-files/): How to scope AI code changes to named files so proposals stay small, predictable and easy to review — with example wording and review checks.
  - [Prompt templates for HTML and CSS changes](https://codingagent.in/guides/prompting-for-code/prompt-templates-for-html-css/): Copy-ready prompt templates for common HTML and CSS changes — new sections, responsive layouts, typography, accessibility fixes — each with scope and checks.
  - [Common AI prompting mistakes in coding (and how to fix them)](https://codingagent.in/guides/prompting-for-code/common-ai-prompting-mistakes/): The most common mistakes when prompting AI for code — vague goals, no file scope, bundled changes, oversharing context — and the fix for each.
- [Editing source files](https://codingagent.in/guides/editing-source-files/): How to organize and edit source files in an AI-assisted workspace: clear file roles, precise edits, consistent naming, encoding and line endings, and safe refactors.
  - [How to organize HTML and CSS project files](https://codingagent.in/guides/editing-source-files/organizing-html-css-project-files/): A simple, scalable file structure for small HTML and CSS projects, with clear file roles that keep AI prompts scoped and diffs small.
  - [Precise code edits and minimal diffs](https://codingagent.in/guides/editing-source-files/precise-code-edits-and-minimal-diffs/): How to make precise code edits that produce minimal, readable diffs: avoid incidental reformatting, keep order, and separate cleanups from changes.
  - [Keeping class names, IDs and links consistent across files](https://codingagent.in/guides/editing-source-files/keeping-class-names-and-links-consistent/): Prevent broken styles and links: how to rename classes, IDs, paths and custom properties safely across HTML and CSS files.
  - [Text encoding, line endings and file integrity](https://codingagent.in/guides/editing-source-files/text-encoding-and-line-endings/): Keep source files compatible across tools: UTF-8 encoding, consistent line endings, no smart quotes in code, and how to spot integrity problems in diffs.
- [Reviewing AI changes](https://codingagent.in/guides/reviewing-ai-changes/): How to review AI-generated code changes: read diffs against your intent, apply selectively, preserve local edits, and catch deletions, dependencies and security risks.
  - [How to read a code diff (for AI-generated changes)](https://codingagent.in/guides/reviewing-ai-changes/how-to-read-a-code-diff/): A beginner-friendly guide to reading code diffs: removed and added lines, files touched, context lines, and what to look for in AI-generated changes.
  - [Preserving your local edits when working with AI](https://codingagent.in/guides/reviewing-ai-changes/preserving-local-edits-with-ai/): How BroCODE preserves local edits, and habits that keep your hand-made changes safe while you review and apply AI proposals.
  - [AI code review checklist for HTML and CSS](https://codingagent.in/guides/reviewing-ai-changes/ai-code-review-checklist/): A practical checklist for reviewing AI-generated HTML and CSS: scope, deletions, dependencies, semantics, accessibility, responsiveness and security.
  - [When to reject an AI proposal (and what to do next)](https://codingagent.in/guides/reviewing-ai-changes/when-to-reject-an-ai-proposal/): Clear signals that an AI code proposal should be rejected, and how to write a narrower follow-up request instead of patching broken code.
- [Checkpoints and recovery](https://codingagent.in/guides/checkpoints-and-recovery/): How to use local checkpoints for reversible experiments in BroCODE: when to capture, how to restore, snapshot limits, and why checkpoints are not backups.
  - [Checkpoints vs backups: what is the difference?](https://codingagent.in/guides/checkpoints-and-recovery/checkpoints-vs-backups/): Checkpoints are local snapshots for undoing experiments; backups are copies stored elsewhere. Why you need both, and how to set up each.
  - [Running safe design experiments with checkpoints](https://codingagent.in/guides/checkpoints-and-recovery/safe-experiments-with-checkpoints/): How to use checkpoints to explore bold design directions safely: checkpoint, branch your thinking, compare and restore.
  - [How to restore an earlier version of your project](https://codingagent.in/guides/checkpoints-and-recovery/restoring-an-earlier-version/): Step-by-step recovery: find the right checkpoint, preserve the current state, restore, and reapply good changes in smaller steps.
  - [Using Git version control alongside checkpoints](https://codingagent.in/guides/checkpoints-and-recovery/version-control-alongside-checkpoints/): How to pair BroCODE’s local checkpoints with Git: export files, commit milestones, and keep a durable history outside the workspace.
- [Static preview](https://codingagent.in/guides/static-preview/): What BroCODE’s V3 static preview does: script-disabled HTML inspection. What it cannot show — frameworks, servers, interactivity — and how to validate outside it.
  - [Script-disabled HTML preview, explained](https://codingagent.in/guides/static-preview/script-disabled-html-preview-explained/): What a script-disabled HTML preview is, why BroCODE V3 uses one, and how to read what you see without over-trusting it.
  - [Testing interactive JavaScript outside the static preview](https://codingagent.in/guides/static-preview/testing-interactive-code-outside-preview/): How to test JavaScript behavior the static preview cannot run: real-browser checks, console errors, keyboard tests and simple automated tests.
  - [Previewing React, Vue and other framework projects](https://codingagent.in/guides/static-preview/previewing-framework-projects/): Why framework projects do not render in BroCODE’s static preview, and how to edit their source in the workspace while building and testing elsewhere.
  - [Validating HTML and accessibility beyond the preview](https://codingagent.in/guides/static-preview/validating-html-and-accessibility/): How to validate HTML and check accessibility after the static preview: validators, keyboard tests, contrast checks, screen readers and Lighthouse.
- [Exports and portability](https://codingagent.in/guides/exports-and-portability/): How BroCODE exports work: ZIP vs JSON, what is included (project files) and omitted (conversation and snapshot history), and how to verify integrity after moving files.
  - [ZIP vs JSON export: which should you choose?](https://codingagent.in/guides/exports-and-portability/zip-vs-json-export/): Compare BroCODE’s ZIP and JSON exports: what each is good for, how each stores files, and how to choose for editors, Git, hosts or scripts.
  - [What BroCODE exports include — and what they omit](https://codingagent.in/guides/exports-and-portability/what-exports-include-and-omit/): Exactly what a BroCODE export contains (your project files) and omits (conversation and snapshot history), and how to keep important context.
  - [Moving a project between BroCODE and other tools](https://codingagent.in/guides/exports-and-portability/moving-projects-between-tools/): How to move source between BroCODE and editors, Git and hosts without losing structure, encoding or context.
  - [Verifying file integrity after export](https://codingagent.in/guides/exports-and-portability/verifying-file-integrity-after-export/): A checklist to confirm an export is complete and intact: file list, encoding, paths, rendering and comparisons between exports.
- [Privacy and safe AI use](https://codingagent.in/guides/privacy-and-safe-ai-use/): How BroCODE handles privacy: local editing stays local, source is sent for AI help only with explicit consent. How to share context deliberately and understand erasure limits.
  - [Consent before sending code to AI: how it works and why](https://codingagent.in/guides/privacy-and-safe-ai-use/consent-before-sending-code-to-ai/): BroCODE sends source for AI help only with explicit consent. What that means, why it matters, and how to decide what to share each time.
  - [Keeping API keys and secrets out of your source code](https://codingagent.in/guides/privacy-and-safe-ai-use/keeping-secrets-out-of-source/): Why secrets should never live in source files, how to keep them out of prompts, exports and published sites, and what to do if one leaks.
  - [Personal data in AI coding prompts: what to avoid](https://codingagent.in/guides/privacy-and-safe-ai-use/personal-data-in-ai-prompts/): How to keep personal data — yours and other people’s — out of AI coding prompts and project files, using placeholders and minimal context.
  - [Understanding erasure limits in local-first AI tools](https://codingagent.in/guides/privacy-and-safe-ai-use/erasure-limits-in-local-ai-tools/): What deleting a local project does and does not do once source has been shared for AI help, and how to plan sharing accordingly.
- [Android workflows](https://codingagent.in/guides/android-workflows/): How to prepare BroCODE projects for Android while the Android release is in preparation: mobile-first source, touch and small screens, and why native release requirements are separate from source exports.
  - [Mobile-first HTML and CSS for small screens](https://codingagent.in/guides/android-workflows/mobile-first-html-css/): A practical guide to mobile-first HTML and CSS: viewport, fluid type, flexible layouts, tap targets and safe areas for Android screens.
  - [Web source vs native Android release: what is the difference?](https://codingagent.in/guides/android-workflows/web-source-vs-native-android-release/): Why a source export is not an Android app, and what a native release adds: packaging, signing, store listing, permissions and policies.
  - [Testing your site on Android browsers](https://codingagent.in/guides/android-workflows/testing-on-android-browsers/): How to test exported web source on Android: real devices, emulation, orientation, text size, dark mode and performance checks.
  - [Touch-friendly interface design for web pages](https://codingagent.in/guides/android-workflows/touch-friendly-interface-design/): Design web pages that work well with fingers: tap target sizes, spacing, no hover-only content, visible states and gesture alternatives.
- [Publishing your project](https://codingagent.in/guides/publishing-your-project/): How to publish a BroCODE project: export reviewed source, choose a static host, deploy, and verify the live site (paths, HTTPS, mobile, SEO, accessibility) before sharing the URL.
  - [Choosing a static host for an HTML and CSS site](https://codingagent.in/guides/publishing-your-project/choosing-a-static-host/): What to look for in a static host for a small HTML/CSS site: HTTPS, custom domains, clean URLs, 404 pages, Git deploys and rollbacks.
  - [Pre-launch checklist for a static website](https://codingagent.in/guides/publishing-your-project/pre-launch-checklist-static-site/): A complete pre-launch checklist for static sites: review, links, assets, metadata, accessibility, performance, privacy and backups.
  - [Verifying a deployed site before sharing the URL](https://codingagent.in/guides/publishing-your-project/verifying-a-deployed-site/): How to verify a live deployment: HTTPS, paths and case sensitivity, mobile and desktop checks, keyboard access, metadata, and Lighthouse on the real URL.
  - [SEO and AI search basics for static sites](https://codingagent.in/guides/publishing-your-project/seo-and-ai-search-basics-for-static-sites/): Make a static site easy for search engines and AI assistants to understand: titles, headings, direct answers, sitemaps, robots.txt, JSON-LD and llms.txt — honestly.
- [Agent safety and verification](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/): A practical, vendor-neutral guide to AI coding agent safety: plan-execute-verify, tests, builds and type checks, sandboxing and tool permissions, human approval gates, prompt injection, audit logs, cost limits and local LLMs.
  - [The plan-execute-verify loop for AI coding](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/plan-execute-verify-loop/): How to structure AI coding work into planning, scoped execution and independent verification, and why a model should never grade its own work.
  - [Verifying AI code changes with tests, builds and type checks](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/tests-builds-and-type-checks/): How unit tests, clean builds and static type checks independently verify AI-generated code, what each catches and what each misses.
  - [Sandboxing, tool permissions and human approval gates for AI agents](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/sandboxing-tool-permissions-and-approval-gates/): How to limit what an AI coding agent can do: sandboxes, allow/ask/deny permission tiers, safe tool-call validation and approval gates for risky actions.
  - [Prompt injection and untrusted content in AI coding](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/prompt-injection-and-untrusted-content/): How prompt injection reaches coding agents through READMEs, issues, dependencies, web pages and tool servers, and the layered defenses that reduce risk.
  - [Audit logs, cost limits and AI agents in CI pipelines](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/audit-logs-cost-limits-and-ci-agents/): How to record AI agent actions for review, cap token spending, and run AI checks in CI/CD pipelines with human oversight.
  - [Running local LLMs for coding with llama.cpp and GGUF](https://codingagent.in/guides/agent-safety-and-verification/running-local-llms-for-coding/): What it takes to run open-weight coding models locally: llama.cpp, GGUF files, quantization, hardware, local servers, and the trade-offs versus hosted models.

## About

- [FAQ](https://codingagent.in/faq/): Straight answers about BroCODE: what it is, how AI proposals work, checkpoints, ZIP/JSON exports, the static preview, privacy, Android release status and pricing.
- [About](https://codingagent.in/about/): What BroCODE is, who it is for, and what this site is: a static, source-grounded demonstration of the V3 AI-assisted coding workflow.
- [Editorial policy](https://codingagent.in/editorial-policy/): How BroCODE guides are written: grounded in the V3 source, no invented features, prices, statistics or reviews, clear limits, and dated updates.
- [Privacy](https://codingagent.in/privacy/): Privacy for this website and a summary of how BroCODE V3 handles your source: local editing, explicit consent before sending code for AI help.
- [Roadmap](https://codingagent.in/roadmap/): planned, not shipped; five iterations with target weeks from start, not dates. Principle: Make every AI action transparent, reversible, and locally controlled.
- [Full text for LLMs](https://codingagent.in/llms-full.txt)
